Phala Phala Mystery

By: Marion Edmunds | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We explore the extraordinary events of one long week in politics in which President Cyril Ramaphosa (may come) came back from the brink

Unique Selling Point:
A week is a long time in politics, and the week that was (and is still to run) has left masses of South Africans confused, frustrated, exasperated and exhausted as the ANC finally brings it's messy, toxic, ideological conflict out into the open. We have a unique opportunity of explaining the events day by day in a ten minute piece which creates a context and understanding for an attack on the Presidency by the RET faction with huge consequences for the entire country, economically, socially, politically and constitutionally. It is a significant inflection point in the country's transition which can be explained through careful interviews with key commentators close to the action. And it's a great story - Disgraced Spy Boss fingers reformer President who has done dodgy deal over a small herd of buffalo with a mysterious Egyptian - Sudanese tycoon, who runs a famous soccer club and sports a trophy South African-born wife on his arm. The fall-out is extraordinary and the ultimate question is how Ramaphosa and the ANC will pull itself out of this mess to face the electorate in the run up to the 2024 elections.

Summary:
PROPOSAL
Late Wednesday, 30 November 2022, the news broke that Parliament should act against President Cyril Ramaphosa in relation to the scandal of the theft of millions of dollars from his farm homestead near Phala Phala under mysterious circumstances. By next week this time, he may be gone from the Presidency, and a new incumbent in the Union buildings, and with that there may come a significant shift in power which fundamentally alters South Africa’s prospects going forward. It’s a political and constitutional crisis, although the shift in power may happen within the ruling ANC party and remains difficult to predict. The country’s fortunes may change completely in the space of a few days. South Africa, and to some extent the whole world, is watching to see what will happen next.

This story will follow the timeline of the week of what has been the most ambitious attack on Cyril Ramaphosa's position from within the ANC, to dislodge him and his reforming agenda from the Presidency over a dodgy buffalo deal he claims to have done. The political scuffle within the ANC which follows the tabling of a report into the theft of dollars from Ramaphosa's Phala Phala farm - allegedly there as as result of the deal - has exposed the extraordinary internal fight for power that until recently has been raging behind closed doors. This is a significant inflection point in the troubled transition which has been rumbling since before 1994, from within the ANC and society at large. Given that we won't get the key players on air, I propose we interview useful experts and do a day by day sort of diary, with explainers so that the viewer has a good grasp of what is alleged to have happened at Phala, what happened when the Section 89 report was tabled, what happened within the ANC thereafter and how the story might play out before the ANC elective conference in mid-December. We will use visuals of the NEC's failed meeting at NASREC on December 1, the debate in Parliament on Tuesday 6 December, any statement by the Presidency, and visuals of Phala Phala and the area near the site of the theft, Cyril's farm. It would also be useful to include tweets by people who are preferring not to be interviews, for example Lindiwe Mazibuko to show the raging twitter debate which is part of this story.

To create a diary effect we can allocate each expert to a particular part of the story


Further information:
We will convene at 5h30 on Monday afternoon, 5 December 2022, to scope the story.

Press Release:


Phala Phala Predicament
A week is a lifetime in South African politics. Since the Phala Phala panel report’s release and President Cyril Ramaphosa’s approach to the Constitutional Court to challenge findings that could lead to his impeachment, speculation as to what will happen next is furiously mounting. It’s a story of great political intrigue: disgraced Spy Boss fingers reformer President who appears to have done a dodgy deal over a small herd of buffalo with a mysterious Egyptian-Sudanese tycoon. And while the President’s opponents both inside and outside of the ANC have used this political crisis to push the veteran politician to the brink, it appears there are more cards to play before the game is cast one way or another. The fall-out from this highly-charged contest has been extraordinary – can Ramaphosa and the ANC pull itself out of this mess to face the electorate in the run up to the 2024 elections? And how will the denouement of the drama shape our future Constitutional state.
Producer: Marion Edmunds | Presenter: Bongani Bingwa

Script:


(VO) THE DRAMA STARTED LATE WEDNESDAY EVENING WHEN AN INDEPENDENT PANEL PROBING THE BIZARRE BURGLARY DROPPED A BOMBSHELL….

Siviwe Gwarube, DA Chief Whip
For the first time you are seeing this breaking news, the President is said to possibly have committed an impeachable offence. It's huge.

Hlengiwe Mkhaliphi, EFF MP
Cyril Ramaphosa didn't see this coming.

(VO IN THEIR LENGTHY REPORT, THE PANEL – COMPRISING SENIOR JURISTS – CLAIMED THAT THE PRESIDENT MIGHT HAVE A CASE TO ANSWER AND COULD EVEN HAVE VIOLATED THE CONSTITUTION.

Professor Richard Calland, Public Law Expert
I was on live television soon after. And what I said was that this was a grave moment for the President, …But I also said that this was Democracy at Work.

(VO) IN PARLIAMENT, POLITICAL PARTIES HAD BEEN WINDING DOWN FOR CHRISTMAS.

BUT NEWS OF THE PANELS’ FINDINGS GOT THEM SCURRYING BACK TO WORK.

HLENGIWE MKHALIPHI IS AN EFF WHIP.

Hlengiwe Mkhaliphi, EFF MP
We are going to accept the report, we are going to discuss the report and we're going to vote for the impeachment to take place.

(VO) THE DA’s CHIEF WHIP SIVIWE GWARUBE WAS FIELDING CALLS.

Siviwe Gwarube, DA Chief Whip
A lot of angst and a lot of anxiety. Even all my own family members were calling and saying, you know, can we afford to impeach a president? Maybe the president is the best that we have?

(VO) RUMOURS CIRCULATED THAT THE PRESIDENT MAY RESIGN, DESPITE HIS DENIALS OF WRONGDOING.

Siviwe Gwarube, DA Chief Whip
If objectively the President is deemed to have broken the law, then we You can't for the sake of stability, and almost as a comfort toy held on to somebody, because we think he is the best that we have.

(VO) THE INITIAL APPLICATION TO PARLIAMENT TO SET UP THE INQUIRY CAME FROM THIS YOUNG MP.
VUYOLWETHU ZUNGULA IS A RELATIVE NEW-COMER TO THE CORRIDORS OF POWER AND ONE OF ONLY TWO MPS REPRESENTING THE ATM PARTY IN THE HOUSE.
AS THE SPONSOR OF THIS REPORT, HE’S BEEN THROWN INTO THE SPOTLIGHT.

Vuyolwethu Zungula, ATM President
I was fortunate to have received a call from one of the members of parliament who say alright, you've won this round. Congratulations, however, be mindful of your security, because you've done what you've done. It is something that is normally done by bigger parties.

(VO)IT WAS A LONG NIGHT OF HEAVY READING.
CONSTITUTIONAL EXPERT RICHARD CALLAND DISSECTED THE LENGTHY REPORT.

Professor Richard Calland, Public Law Expert
I became quite troubled, because I felt that it was not of the impeccable standard that such a report needs to be if it is going to be the springboard for the full impeachment process.

(VO)THE PANEL BALANCED RAMAPHOSA’S EXPLANATIONS AGAINST A
VERSION OF EVENTS SUPPLIED BY SOUTH AFRICA’S FORMER SPY BOSS ARTHUR FRASER, THE CONTROVERSIAL CIVIL SERVANT WHO FIRST SET THE CAT AMONG THE PIGEONS SIX MONTHS AGO.

Bongani Bingwa PTC: Arthur Fraser came to this police station in Johannesburg to lay criminal charges against the sitting president. He was armed with affidavits, footage bank accounts, and he claimed that millions of dollars had been stolen from a hiding place and a couch at the President's farm and that by not reporting the incident to the police, as well as other crimes, the President had broken the law.

(VO) THREE HOURS DRIVE NORTH FROM JOHANNESBURG, RAMAPHOSA’S LIMPOPO FARM HAS NOW BECOME A PLACE OF MEDIA INTEREST - AND SECURITY HAS BEEN JACKED UP AS CARTE BLANCHE FOUND WHEN WE VISITED THIS WEEK, MAKING IT DIFFICULT TO FIELD INQUIRIES.

Policeman sound up : or look at someone someone's property please…

Bongani Bingwa: What did you expect Cyril Ramaphosa to do once the report, this independent panel report came up?
Vuyolwethu Zungula: Resign.
(VO) THE LONGER RAMAPHOSA STAYED OUT OF SIGHT, THE GREATER THE SPECULATION OF HIS DEMISE.

Siviwe Gwarube, DA Chief Whip
We had a parliamentary sitting in the very next day on the Thursday, and you could see cabinet ministers, you know, walking in and out speaking in hushed tones. There was you know, worry and fear.

Professor Richard Calland, Public Law Expert
But what then happened over the following few hours was that someone and some people managed to stiffen his resolve. His backward bone was located so to speak.

(VO) RAMAPHOSA’S OPPONENTS WITHIN HIS OWN PARTY HAD ALREADY CALLED ON HIM TO STEP ASIDE.

A SCHEDULED MEETING OF THE INFLUENTIAL NATIONAL EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE WAS ON THE CARDS IN JOHANNESBURG

PTC Bongani Bingwa: “Farmgate” as it had become known brought the ANC’s internal factional battles, always bubbling under the surface, wide open.

(VO) THIS VETERAN ZUMA LOYALIST NOTWITHSTANDING, THE MEETING WAS POSTPONED, RAMAPHOSA LIVED ANOTHER DAY.

BUT, SAYS POLITICAL AUTHOR MPUMELELO MKHABELA, HIS REPUTATION HAS SUFFERED.

Mpumelelo Mkhabela
Political Commentator
He rose into power..eh eh with the context that he was going undo all the corruption that we've come to associate with Zuma, and the ANC. So now that he's implicated in a scandal of this nature, he just becomes like all the ordinary people. … He can't be expected to lead the ANC morally into higher ground.

(VO)SOUTH AFRICA WAS ONCE AGAIN ON TENTERHOOKS, AS THE ANC WRESTLED WITH ITS OPTIONS. SONGEZO ZIBI HEADS A POLITICAL THINKTANK.

Songezo Zibi
Founder of the Rivonia Circle
President Cyril Ramaphosa’s popularity with voters exceeds that of the ANC. That means excuse the pun, he is their trump card amongst the ANC base. …The dilemma the ANC faces is that he was last chance saloon, it is tainted already after him, it is tickets, Bongani… I think this scandal puts the dominance of the ANC in South African politics in peril, and potentially could make it a thing of the past.


(VO) BY NOW, INTRIGUING PUZZLE PIECES HAD BEEN ADDED TO THE OPAQUE PICTURE.

A DUBAI-BASED SUDANESE TYCOON, HAZIM MUSTAFA, REPORTEDLY CONFIRMED RAMAPHOSA’S STORY OF A BUFFALO SALE, STATING THAT HE’D PAID 580-THOUSAND DOLLARS, NOT MILLIONS.

BUT THE ANIMALS WERE NEVER SHIPPED.

Songezo Zibi
Founder of the Rivonia Circle
What muddies is the waters is that it appears on almost every submission that gets made is laughable .. like even this gentleman that claims to have bought the buffalos, he belatedly wants a refund now, but hey man, who is gonna believe that? I don't sorry, I don't believe it.

Bongan Bingwai: At least he exists.

Songezo Zibi: At least he exists right!

(VO) HAZIM MUSTAFA HAS A CONNECTION TO THIS COUNTRY - HIS FASHIONABLE SOUTH AFRICAN WIFE.

BUT HE TOLD REPORTERS THAT HE DID’NT KNOW THE LIVE-STOCK HAD EVEN BELONGED TO THE PRESIDENT

(VO) MEANWHILE, THOSE TRACKING THE CONSTITUTIONAL NARRATIVE WERE HEARING THE FAINT RUMBLE OF A NEW LINE OF DEFENCE.

THE BIG LEGAL GUNS WERE COMING – STRAIGHT TO THE CONSTITUTIONAL COURT.

Bongani Bingwa PTC: President Ramaphosa has approached the highest court in the land directly seeking for the section 89 Report to be reviewed. He says the panel misunderstood its brief. And so he's engaged the country's most senior judges.

THE ATM PRESIDENT IS OUTRAGED.

Vuyolwethu Zungula, ATM President
He cited myself. He cited the three members of the panel. He even cited Parliament as an institution, simply because he wants to send a very strong message that I'm going to take you to court

(VO) AND ON THE SEVENTH DAY THE PRESIDENT EMERGED AT AN OFFICIAL ENGAGEMENT – HIS FIRST PUBLIC APPEARANCE IN A WEEK. BUT THE DOLLAR HEIST HAS SPAWNED OTHER INVESTIGATIONS

Mpumelelo Mkhabela
Political Commentator
So the dilemma here is that South Africa might have a president who continuously is facing these type of investigations, which might clear him in the end, but it doesn't take away the fact that there's a cloud in the meantime.

(VO) IN A FEW DAYS, RAMAPHOSA WILL FACE UP TO THE ANC ELECTIVE CONFERENCE WHERE HIS LEADERSHIP IS NOT ASSURED.

BUT BEFORE THAT, HE MUST FACE A DIVIDED PARLIAMENT WHICH WILL VOTE ON WHETHER TO ADOPT THIS CONTROVERSIAL REPORT - OR FOR NOW, LET THE FISH OFF THE HOOK.


Phala Phala PROMO Script for VIEWING

PROMO 11 Second
(VO) ONE REPORT, SEVEN DAYS, AND A COMPROMISED PRESIDENT - THE STORY OF SOUTH AFRICA’S POLITICAL ROLLERCOASTER WEEK



PROMO 1

Hlengiwe Mkhaliphi, EFF MP
Cyril Ramaphosa didn't see this coming,
ONE WEEK - WHICH TOOK THE PRESIDENT TO THE BRINK…AND BROUGHT HIM BACK AGAIN
Siviwe Gwarube, DA Chief Whip
I think this is gonna go down in history, that when institutions like Parliament work, you can actually hold the executive to account

PROMO 2
THE CURIOUS CASE OF THE CASH IN THE COUCH PUTS PRESIDENT RAMAPHOSA IN THE FIRING LINE
PROMO BITES
Mpumelelo Mkhabela
Political Commentator
It's now about who is least corrupt compared to the other, so that's the space we are in.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We explore the extraordinary events of one long week in politics in which President Cyril Ramaphosa (may come) came back from the brink
metadata.Unique Selling Point: A week is a long time in politics, and the week that was (and is still to run) has left masses of South Africans confused, frustrated, exasperated and exhausted as the ANC finally brings it's messy, toxic, ideological conflict out into the open. We have a unique opportunity of explaining the events day by day in a ten minute piece which creates a context and understanding for an attack on the Presidency by the RET faction with huge consequences for the entire country, economically, socially, politically and constitutionally. It is a significant inflection point in the country's transition which can be explained through careful interviews with key commentators close to the action. And it's a great story - Disgraced Spy Boss fingers reformer President who has done dodgy deal over a small herd of buffalo with a mysterious Egyptian - Sudanese tycoon, who runs a famous soccer club and sports a trophy South African-born wife on his arm. The fall-out is extraordinary and the ultimate question is how Ramaphosa and the ANC will pull itself out of this mess to face the electorate in the run up to the 2024 elections.
metadata.Summary: PROPOSAL Late Wednesday, 30 November 2022, the news broke that Parliament should act against President Cyril Ramaphosa in relation to the scandal of the theft of millions of dollars from his farm homestead near Phala Phala under mysterious circumstances. By next week this time, he may be gone from the Presidency, and a new incumbent in the Union buildings, and with that there may come a significant shift in power which fundamentally alters South Africa’s prospects going forward. It’s a political and constitutional crisis, although the shift in power may happen within the ruling ANC party and remains difficult to predict. The country’s fortunes may change completely in the space of a few days. South Africa, and to some extent the whole world, is watching to see what will happen next. This story will follow the timeline of the week of what has been the most ambitious attack on Cyril Ramaphosa's position from within the ANC, to dislodge him and his reforming agenda from the Presidency over a dodgy buffalo deal he claims to have done. The political scuffle within the ANC which follows the tabling of a report into the theft of dollars from Ramaphosa's Phala Phala farm - allegedly there as as result of the deal - has exposed the extraordinary internal fight for power that until recently has been raging behind closed doors. This is a significant inflection point in the troubled transition which has been rumbling since before 1994, from within the ANC and society at large. Given that we won't get the key players on air, I propose we interview useful experts and do a day by day sort of diary, with explainers so that the viewer has a good grasp of what is alleged to have happened at Phala, what happened when the Section 89 report was tabled, what happened within the ANC thereafter and how the story might play out before the ANC elective conference in mid-December. We will use visuals of the NEC's failed meeting at NASREC on December 1, the debate in Parliament on Tuesday 6 December, any statement by the Presidency, and visuals of Phala Phala and the area near the site of the theft, Cyril's farm. It would also be useful to include tweets by people who are preferring not to be interviews, for example Lindiwe Mazibuko to show the raging twitter debate which is part of this story. To create a diary effect we can allocate each expert to a particular part of the story
